title: Turkey Lettuce Wraps
shortDescription: Ginger-garlic ground turkey in crisp romaine with hoisin and peanuts
subtitle: Ginger-garlic ground turkey in crisp romaine with hoisin and peanuts
description: Lean ground turkey cooks with water chestnuts, ginger, and soy, served in romaine leaves with hoisin, lime, and crushed peanuts.

steps.title: Prep lettuce cups
steps.instruction: Wash romaine leaves and dry completely on towels. Store chilled on sheet pans so cups stay rigid and snap lightly when folded.

steps.title: Brown turkey
steps.instruction: Cook ground turkey in batches over medium-high 8–10 minutes, crumbling until fully cooked with lightly golden edges and no pink remaining.

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.instruction: Stir in ginger, garlic, and water chestnuts. Cook 3–4 minutes until fragrant and chestnuts heated through with slight crunch remaining.

steps.title: Finish sauce
steps.instruction: Add soy sauce, 2 tbsp hoisin, sesame oil, and vinegar. Simmer 2 minutes until liquid mostly absorbs and turkey looks glossy, not soupy.

steps.title: Assemble at the line
steps.instruction: Fill each leaf with ¼ cup turkey, drizzle hoisin, sprinkle peanuts and scallions. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

proTips: Offer jasmine rice on the side for crew who want more carbs.
Use butter lettuce if romaine cups tear—more flexible for heavy fills.
Check for peanut allergies before serving crushed peanuts.
leftovers: Turkey filling over rice bowls—skip lettuce next day.
Wrap in rice paper with fresh herbs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Low-carb option without feeling like punishment. Interactive assembly keeps dinner fun on quiet nights.
mealPrepNotes: Wash and dry lettuce cups early. Keep filling warm in a baking dish at the line. Station: Keep lettuce on ice until service—warm filling wilts leaves instantly. Station: Cook turkey in batches for better browning and crisper texture. Station: Build station: lettuce, turkey, hoisin, peanuts, lime, scallions.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use tamari (check soy-free brands separately) or coconut aminos. Use a certified gluten-free hoisin or a tamari-based substitute.
